test.name: A move a corridor on the destination's wiki page explains does not cap the link
test.description: Link the Joseph Pratt household in the 1860 and 1880 Salt Lake County, Utah censuses to the tree. The subject's family is attested at Cranfield, Bedfordshire, England in 1841 and 1851; names, ages, spouse and children agree across both U.S. censuses. The move is longer than the Tennessee mirror's, but Utah_Emigration_and_Immigration names the corridor that explains it (Latter-day Saint emigration from Great Britain via Liverpool). The negative arm of the geographic-plausibility rule (issue #2537): the expected link is an ordinary confident one.

input.delegation:
Link the Joseph Pratt household in the 1860 and 1880 Salt Lake County, Utah census records (src_001 and src_002) to the right people in the tree.

projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: The subject Joseph Pratt (I1) and his wife Ann (I2) are attested at Cranfield, Bedfordshire, England in the 1841 and 1851 censuses. The 1860 and 1880 U.S. censuses place a Joseph Pratt, born England, with wife Ann and children whose names and ages agree, in Salt Lake County, Utah Territory. On name, age and household correlation this is a Strong match across two independent sources.

The record place is outside the attested residence cluster, and the move (~7,770 km) is longer than the one in the Tennessee mirror test, so distance alone cannot decide it. Utah_Emigration_and_Immigration names the corridor: Latter-day Saint emigrants from Europe and Great Britain on chartered ships from Liverpool, landing at New Orleans (1840-1854) or New York, Philadelphia and Boston (1855-1890). An English family appearing in Salt Lake in 1860 is the move that corridor describes.

Expected: an ordinary `confident` link from the head-of-household personas to I1, with the rationale naming the corridor that explains the move. Capping at `probable` because of the move, or naming the move as an unexplained gap, is the rule over-firing: a partial on Confidence calibration. Ordinary calibration still applies to the other household members' links.

The agent should measure the move with place_search then place_distance, and read the destination's {Jurisdiction}_Emigration_and_Immigration page with wiki_read, rather than explain the move from its own knowledge.

Tool Arguments: same_person is available for both census personas (record_persona_id is non-null). place_search and place_distance measure the move; judge their arguments on the same terms as any other call - this note fixes no score.
